Senator Bennet’s push for a “robust” Farm Bill ignores the real issue: Washington’s addiction to bloated spending. The Department of Agriculture’s budget ballooned from $150B to $203B since 2019—yet farmers still face skyrocketing costs and bureaucratic hurdles. Conservation programs like EQIP and CSP funnel billions into administrative overhead while small producers struggle.

The Farm Bill’s nutrition title—its most expensive component—diverts resources to SNAP expansions instead of addressing core agricultural needs like supply chain resilience or cutting input costs. Real reform would slash red tape, prioritize market-driven solutions, and stop using farmers as pawns for social welfare agendas.

Until D.C. stops treating agriculture like a piggy bank for pet projects, no amount of funding will fix systemic waste.
